# Company profile: the deck

PR 4 of the company profile (the data, the editor and the versions are PR 1; the design and the PDF are
PR 2; the logo library and the introduction letter are PR 3). This is the same profile as slides: a
**twenty-four slide animated PowerPoint deck**, English and French, generated by HQ from the published
version and downloaded beside the PDF.

`docs/COMPANY_PROFILE.md` is the engine — the content, the versions, the editor, the downloads.
`docs/company-profile/DESIGN.md` is the book. This is its sibling at a different pace: same contract,
same type, same colour, same restraint, a different format and a different speed.

---

## Where it is

HQ › Company profile. **Download deck** sits next to **Download** on the editor and on a version's
preview; the versions list carries PDF EN / PDF FR / Deck EN / Deck FR on every row.

```
/company-profile/deck?locale=en                 the published version, in English
/company-profile/deck?locale=fr&version=3       version 3, for someone who may edit or approve
```

Route name `company-profile.deck`, behind `company_profile.view`, exactly like the PDF — and the two
share the code that resolves the version, so a draft cannot leak through one of them and not the other.
The filename follows the PDF's with its own extension:

```
JBS Praxis company profile JBS-CP-2026-11-v1 EN.pptx
```

A download is about **40 milliseconds** and the file is about **200 KB**. Both are audited:
`COMPANY_PROFILE_DECK_DOWNLOADED`.

```
php artisan company-profile:deck              both languages, into storage/app/company-profile
php artisan company-profile:deck fr --fit     measure every French slide and say what overflows
```

---

## How it is built, and why not with a library

The owner asked for a template designed once and filled by HQ, with **real transitions and entrance
builds** — Morph where it helps, with a sensible fallback. PhpPresentation cannot author an entrance
animation or a Morph transition at all, so it is not used. The deck writes PresentationML directly.

| Piece | Where | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| The template | `praxis_core/resources/company-profile/deck/parts/` | every fixed part of the package as a file: the content types, the package relationships, docProps, the presentation and its relationships, the theme, the master and the one blank layout |
| The design | `App\Support\CompanyProfile\Deck\Style` | the slide, the twelve-column grid, the palette, the type scale and the floors |
| The slides | `App\Support\CompanyProfile\Deck\Blueprint` | the twenty-four slides: what each reads, where it puts it, how it moves |
| The shapes | `App\Support\CompanyProfile\Deck\Slide` | text, hairline, Praxis rule, bar stack, picture, Ink ground — and the boxes they occupy |
| The motion | `App\Support\CompanyProfile\Deck\Animate` | `<p:timing>` and `<p:transition>` |
| The fit | `App\Support\CompanyProfile\Deck\Metrics`, `Fit` | measured line breaking, and whether every slide fits |
| The package | `App\Support\CompanyProfile\Deck\DeckRenderer`, `Zip` | the parts, the media, and the archive |

**The template is copied in untouched**, except docProps, which take this profile's title, version and
date. Only `ppt/slides/slideN.xml`, its relationships and `ppt/media/*` are written per render.

### The zip is ours

The live web PHP has no `ext-zip` — the ground `docs/DOCUMENTS.md` section 3 found for `gd` and
`imagick` — and neither has the Laragon PHP this was built on, so `Deck\Zip` writes the archive itself:
local headers, raw deflate through zlib, a central directory and an end record. It reads one too, which
is what the tests open the file with. **Nothing in the deck calls `ZipArchive`**, and nothing should: a
test that leant on it would be testing a machine the deck will never run on. Every entry carries a fixed
timestamp, so the same profile in the same language renders to the same bytes twice.

### No gd either

`Deck\Images` reads a PNG's `IHDR` and a JPEG's frame header for their sizes. SVG is deliberately not
read: PowerPoint places an SVG only beside a raster copy of it, and nothing on the server can make one.
A logo with no PNG is left off the wall rather than placed as something it is not — the rule the PDF
keeps for the same reason.

---

## Fonts: Georgia and Arial, and why

The deck is opened by people we do not control, on Windows, on macOS, sometimes in Google Slides. Two
ways to survive that: embed the brand faces, or design to faces everyone already has.

**It designs to Georgia and Arial**, and embeds nothing. Not a compromise — the brand's own declared
fallbacks (`docs/BRAND.md` section 8: *"Newsreader", "Newsreader Fallback", Georgia, serif* and
*"Plus Jakarta Sans", …, Arial, sans-serif*). Georgia speaks and Arial works, which is the brand's own
division of labour. The reasons, in order:

- **Google Slides ignores embedded fonts entirely** and substitutes. A deck designed to Newsreader
  metrics and drawn in a substitute reflows, and a reflowed slide at this density runs off the bottom.
- **macOS PowerPoint reads embedded fonts inconsistently**, so the same deck would be two decks.
- Embedding four cuts is several hundred KB on a file that is 200 KB.
- Georgia and Arial are present on Windows, on macOS and in Google Slides' own font list, so the deck
  renders identically in all three with nothing to load and nothing to substitute.

Their advance widths are committed as `resources/company-profile/deck/deck-metrics.json`, read out of
the TrueType files once by `resources/company-profile/deck/tools/ttf-widths.php`. **Nothing in the
application opens a font file.** Rebuild the table only when the deck takes a new face or a new
character:

```
php resources/company-profile/deck/tools/ttf-widths.php > resources/company-profile/deck/deck-metrics.json
```

---

## The type, and the floors

| Role | Face | Size / leading |
|---|---|---|
| Cover line | Georgia | 48 / 56, −0.01em |
| Section statement | Georgia | 37 / 45 |
| Slide title | Georgia | 29 / 35 |
| Sub-head: pillar, practice, team, client | Georgia | 19.5 / 24.5 |
| Domain | Georgia | 16.5 / 21 |
| Lead | Arial | 16 / 24 |
| Body | Arial | 12.5 / 19 |
| Small body | Arial | 11.5 / 17 |
| Label | Arial bold | 11.5 / 17 |
| Caption | Arial | 10 / 14 |
| Running reference | Arial | 8.5 / 12 |

Three floors, because three kinds of thing are set: **reading text never below 11.5pt**, labels never
below 10pt, the running reference in the foot — chrome, meant to be ignorable — never below 8.5pt.

**French is never bought by shrinking.** PowerPoint is given `<a:noAutofit/>`, so it will not rescue
anything; the deck measures every block with the real Georgia and Arial widths and `Deck\Fit` refuses to
write a file whose slide overflows. The fix for an overflow is the blueprint — fewer items on the slide,
or shorter copy — never the scale. `DeckRendererTest` holds that line in both languages.

## Colour and the grid

16:9 at 960 × 540pt. Twelve columns on a 16pt gutter, 64pt side margins, 54pt head, 52pt foot. The
palette is `docs/BRAND.md` section 7: Ink `#0C142B` for headings, Slate `#4A5468` for body, Muted
`#5E6679` for captions, hairlines `#C5CCD6`, and the teal family as a signal rather than a wash. Two
slides are Ink.

---

## The devices

**The Praxis rule is the continuity.** A section opener draws it under its statement; every slide of
that section carries the same rule, higher up, heading its content. Because it is shapes 2 and 3 on
every slide of the family, the **Morph** transition slides it from one position to the next, and the
section's one graphic element holds the family together. On the problem slides it is Ink across the
width of the problems and turns Teal exactly where the answers begin; on the Praxis Method its split
falls between *Design* and *Build* — the point where the thinking becomes the thing, which is what
praxis means.

**The build is the argument.** On a problem slide the problems arrive before their answers. On the
method the stages arrive in order. On the cover the bar stack draws bar by bar.

Everything else that separates is a 0.75pt hairline.

---

## The motion

`docs/BRAND.md` section 11 is the brief: things settle, they do not perform. No bounce, no spin, no
glow. Three entrances and nothing else:

| Name | What it does | Where |
|---|---|---|
| `fade` | opacity only | a block that simply needs to be there |
| `rise` | a fade with a lift of a fortieth of the slide | the one thing a slide is about |
| `wipe` | left to right | the Praxis rule and the hairlines, which draw to join a question to its answer |

Every slide **builds itself when it arrives** — every effect is "after previous", so a presenter walks
the deck with one key and never waits mid-slide. Transitions are **Morph** between the slides of a
section and a **700–800ms fade** everywhere else. Morph lives in a namespace PowerPoint 2016
introduced, so it is written inside an `mc:AlternateContent` with a fade underneath it: Google Slides,
LibreOffice and PowerPoint 2013 read the fade and the deck still moves.

The timing XML is the shape PowerPoint itself writes. It was read out of a file PowerPoint saved rather
than written from the specification, because the specification allows several encodings of "after
previous" and only one of them round-trips. If you change `Deck\Animate`, check the result by opening
the deck in PowerPoint and reading the animation pane, not by reading the schema.

## The twenty-four slides

Every slide carries the running reference in the foot. Sizes in the *reads* column are the contract's
own keys (`company-profile/CONTRACT.md`).

| # | Slide | Reads | Moves |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Cover** | `cover.headline`, `cover.descriptor`, `meta` | the lockup fades, the line rises, the bar stack draws bar by bar, the descriptor fades |
| 2 | **Point of view** — the statement | `pov.title` | the statement rises, the rule draws Ink then Teal |
| 3 | **Point of view** — the argument | `pov.title`, `pov.paragraphs` (3) | Morph: the statement shrinks into a heading and the rule slides up; the argument rises |
| 4 | **What we build** — the statement | `system.title`, `system.lead` | statement rises, rule draws, lead fades |
| 5 | **The pillars**, 1–2 | `system.pillars[0..1]` | each hairline wipes, then its pillar rises |
| 6 | **The pillars**, 3–4 | `system.pillars[2..3]` | Morph from slide 5; the same build |
| 7 | **The hard problems** — the opener | `problems.title`, `problems.lead` | statement rises, rule draws, lead fades |
| 8 | **Problems**, domains 1–2 | `problems.groups[0..1]` | each domain fades, then every problem fades and its answer rises |
| 9 | **Problems**, domains 3–4 | `problems.groups[2..3]` | Morph; the same build |
| 10 | **Problems**, domains 5–6 | `problems.groups[4..5]` | Morph; the same build |
| 11 | **The closing line** (Ink) | `problems.closing` | the line rises, the rule draws in white then Bright Teal |
| 12 | **Practices** — the opener | `practices.title`, `practices.lead` | statement rises, rule draws, lead fades |
| 13 | **Practices**, 1–2 | `practices.items[0..1]` (`name`, `summary`, `capabilities`) | hairline wipes, the practice rises, what it covers fades |
| 14 | **Practices**, 3–4 | `practices.items[2..3]` | Morph; the same build |
| 15 | **The Praxis Method** | `method.title`, `method.lead`, `method.stages` | the head rises, the rule draws with its split between Design and Build, the four stages rise in order |
| 16 | **The principles** | `method.principles` | Morph; each hairline wipes and its principle rises |
| 17 | **Teams** — the opener | `teams.title`, `teams.lead` | statement rises, rule draws, lead fades |
| 18 | **Teams**, 1–2 | `teams.items[0..1]`: `name`, `summary`, `disciplines`, `experience`, **held** `credentials` | hairline wipes, the team rises, its detail fades |
| 19 | **Teams**, 3–4 | `teams.items[2..3]` | Morph; the same build |
| 20 | **Selected work** — the opener and the first three | `work.title`, `work.lead`, `work.items[0..2]` | the head rises, the rule draws, each hairline wipes and its case rises |
| 21 | **Selected work** — the other three | `work.items[3..5]` | Morph; the same build |
| 22 | **Clients** | `clients.title`, `clients.logos` (the library's deck set) | the head rises, the rule draws, the wall fades in, 70ms apart |
| 23 | **Security and company facts** (Ink) | `security.title`, `security.items`, `facts.title`, **enabled** `facts.items` | the head rises, the rule draws in white then Bright Teal, the items fade, the facts rise |
| 24 | **Back cover** | `contact.*`, `meta` | the call rises, the rule draws, the contact fades, the hairline wipes, the closing line rises |

A case shows its client, its sector, its own line and what the system changed. **The problem it started
from and what was built for it are in the proposal**, where a reader who has got this far will ask for
them — the same decision the book made, for the same reason.

### The wall

`clients.logos` comes from the HQ logo library (`docs/COMPANY_PROFILE.md` section 9), which keeps a
**transparent PNG** of every logo for exactly this and knows which logos are ticked for the deck rather
than for the book. The deck asks it for `forProfile('deck')`. A wall is never worth a failed download,
so with no library — a preview off the seed, a test with no database — it falls back to what the
contract carries, and then to the clients the profile itself names in its work, set in the serif at
sub-head size so the slide still reads as a wall. Nothing invents a client or renames one. A logo the
library has no PNG for keeps its name and loses its mark, which is the rule the book keeps for SVGs
dompdf cannot draw.

**Matched on area, not on height.** Logos arrive at every proportion, and scaling them all to one
height makes a wide wordmark shout and a square mark whisper. `Deck\Images::box()` gives every mark the
same optical area (2400pt²) and then clamps it to its cell and to a 52pt band, so a mark too tall for
the band is held to the band rather than breaking the row. The book learnt this first
(`App\Support\CompanyProfile\Assets::logoBox`); this is the same rule with the deck's own reader.

The committed previews are rendered from the seed, which carries no logos, so slide 22 shows the
fallback there. `deck-previews/en-22-with-logos.jpg` is the same slide rendered with twelve marks on
the library, which is what sales will see.

---

## The rules the file keeps

The same rules the PDF keeps, tested in `tests/Feature/CompanyProfile/DeckRendererTest.php` against the
text in the slide parts, not against the editor:

- a credential whose `held` is not `true` never reaches a slide;
- a fact whose `enabled` is not `true` never reaches a slide, and the Cameroon entity is off by default;
- nobody is named — teams are described by discipline, experience and the credentials they hold;
- "squad" and "deployed" (and their French equivalents) do not appear;
- the pharmaceutical client is never named;
- no price anywhere: no currency symbol beside a figure, no currency code;
- French spacing never asks for a glyph the deck has no width for — `App\Support\CompanyProfile\Typography`
  turns the brand's narrow no-break space into one Georgia and Arial both carry.

`tests/Feature/CompanyProfile/ProfileDownloadDeckTest.php` covers the other half: the route, the
permission, both languages, the filename, and that a draft needs edit or approve.

---

## Proofing it

```
php artisan company-profile:deck                    writes both decks
php artisan company-profile:deck --fit              measures both and writes nothing
```

`docs/company-profile/deck-previews/` holds every slide as an image in both languages, plus a contact
sheet per language and `en-22-with-logos.jpg`, the wall with marks on it. They are rendered by opening the deck in PowerPoint and exporting PNGs, then
scaling them; **a renderer is not part of the app**.

**What a still frame cannot show:** the previews are the final frame of every slide, so they show the
composition and nothing of the motion — not the Morph between the slides of a section (the rule sliding
from under a statement to the head of the content), not the order a slide builds in, and not the
transitions. To see those, open the file and press F5.

## Changing it

- **A slide's content or its build** → `Deck\Blueprint`, and this document's table in the same commit.
- **The look** — type, colour, grid, floors → `Deck\Style`. Nothing else carries a measurement.
- **A new kind of shape** → `Deck\Slide`.
- **The motion vocabulary** → `Deck\Animate`, then check it in PowerPoint's animation pane.
- **The package's fixed parts** — theme, master, layout, presentation → the files under
  `resources/company-profile/deck/parts/`. The slide count is written into three of them
  (`[Content_Types].xml`, `ppt/presentation.xml`, `ppt/_rels/presentation.xml.rels`) as well as into
  `Blueprint::SLIDES`, so changing it means changing all four.

After any change: `php artisan company-profile:deck --fit` in both languages, then open both files.
